problems.location: Concept 3: Evidence-Based Cognitive Strategies for Retention and Conceptual Transfer / block 5
problems.lesson_text: While self-explanation and discovery-based approaches accelerate understanding in learners with adequate background schemas, they can impair performance when prior knowledge is absent (Ionas et al., 2012; Alfieri et al., 2011). Novices require direct scaffolding, worked examples, and structured contrast before unguided generative exploration becomes effective.
problems.source_text: Research has shown that allowing learners to experiment on their own, with no guidance (unassisted discovery), does not improve learning outcomes (Alfieri et al., 2011).
problems.reason: The source cites Alfieri for the finding that unguided discovery does not improve outcomes, while the lesson credits it with discovery helping learners who have background knowledge (the prior-knowledge finding is only about self-explanation, from Ionas).
